title: Connections Levi Civita and Parallel Transport

items.title: Connection on a smooth vector bundle
items.statement:
Let $E\to M$ be a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle on a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold; manifolds with boundary are allowed. Write $\Gamma(E)$ for its smooth sections, as in [[def-smooth-section-local-section-and-support]]. Define
$$\Omega^1(M;E)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Hom}(TM,E)).$$
The Hom bundle is the smooth bundle supplied by [[thm-dual-and-hom-transition-functions-define-smooth-bundles]]. Thus an element $\eta$ assigns a linear map $\eta_p:T_pM\to E_p$ to each point, smoothly in bundle charts. This is also the meaning of an $E$-valued one-form, customarily written as a section of $T^*M\otimes E$. No tangent-only tensor construction is needed for this definition.

A **connection** on $E$ is an $\mathbb R$-linear map $\nabla:\Gamma(E)\to\Omega^1(M;E)$ such that, for every $f\in C^\infty(M)$ and $s\in\Gamma(E)$,
$$\nabla(fs)=df\otimes s+f\nabla s.$$
Here $(df\otimes s)_p(v)=df_p(v)s(p)$, using [[def-differential-of-a-smooth-real-valued-function]]. In local coordinates and a local frame of $E$, this map has entries $(\partial_i f)s^a$, so it is a smooth Hom-bundle section. The tensor notation in the rule therefore already has a defined meaning.

This definition specifies a given operator, not its existence. It uses no choice axiom. If $M$ is empty or $E$ has rank zero, both spaces are zero spaces and there is exactly one such operator. If $M$ has dimension zero, $TM$ is the zero bundle and the same conclusion holds, even when $E$ has positive rank. Rank one uses the same definition without a preferred trivialization.
items.proof_plan: For a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle E on M, a connection is an R-linear operator Gamma(E)->Gamma(T*M tensor E) with nabla(fs)=df tensor s+f nabla(s). Define E-valued one-forms here as smooth fibrewise linear maps TM->E, with local components; arbitrary-bundle tensor construction must be checked against the existing bundle interfaces.

items.title: Covariant derivative of a section in a vector field direction
items.statement:
For a connection as in [[def-connection-on-a-smooth-vector-bundle]], a smooth vector field $X\in\Gamma(TM)$ and a section $s\in\Gamma(E)$, define the **covariant derivative in direction $X$** by
$$
abla_Xs=(
abla s)(X),\qquad (
abla_Xs)(p)=(
abla s)_p(X(p)).$$
It is a smooth section: in any local coordinates and bundle frame, if the matrix of $
abla s$ has entries $b^a_i$ and $X$ has components $X^i$, its components are the finite sums $\sum_i b^a_iX^i$. For a single tangent vector $v\in T_pM$, the notation $
abla_vs$ means $(
abla s)_p(v)$. In particular the direction is used only at $p$, while the section can be differentiated there.

Zero direction gives zero; zero section gives zero by real linearity of $
abla$. For a zero-dimensional base the sum is empty. Empty base and rank-zero bundle also give the unique zero section. A direction is not required to be nonzero or to extend along any prescribed curve. This is evaluation of supplied data and needs no choice.
items.proof_plan: Evaluate the E-valued one-form nabla(s) on the vector field X to define nabla_X s. This is smooth in local components and additive over R.

items.title: Connection laws in directional form
items.statement:
The directional operator of a connection obeys
$$
abla_{fX+gY}s=f
abla_Xs+g
abla_Ys,\qquad 
abla_X(as+bt)=a
abla_Xs+b
abla_Xt,$$
$$
abla_X(fs)=X(f)s+f
abla_Xs$$
for smooth functions $f,g$, real numbers $a,b$, vector fields $X,Y$ and sections $s,t$. Conversely, a map $D:\Gamma(TM)	imes\Gamma(E)	o\Gamma(E)$ with these three laws comes from a unique connection by evaluation. This includes manifolds with boundary.
items.proof_plan: Evaluation is C-infinity-linear in X. Evaluating the defining Leibniz formula on X gives nabla_X(fs)=X(f)s+f nabla_Xs. Conversely these directional laws and smooth local components recover the one-form operator.

items.title: A bundle connection is local and restricts to open sets
items.statement: For a connection on $E\to M$, if two sections agree near $p$, their covariant derivatives at $p$ agree in every tangent direction. The derivative in direction $X$ depends only on $X(p)$. For every open $U\subseteq M$, there is a unique connection on $E|_U$ agreeing with the original on restricted global sections; restrictions to nested open sets compose. Boundary points are included.
items.proof_plan: If s vanishes near p choose a bump chi supported there with chi(p)=1. From 0=nabla_X(chi s)(p)=Xchi(p)s(p)+chi(p)nabla_Xs(p) infer nabla_Xs(p)=0; no derivative-zero strengthening of the bump statement is needed. Multiply a local section by a bump equal to one on a smaller neighbourhood (supplied by the chart-bump proof) and extend by zero. The vanishing argument makes the restricted derivative independent of extension; local formulas give smoothness and uniqueness. Directional dependence only on X(p) follows directly from evaluating the E-valued one-form.

items.title: Connection one form in a local frame
items.statement:
Let $e=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ be a local frame of $E$ on an open set $U$, in the sense of [[def-local-frame-and-global-frame-of-a-vector-bundle]]. Restrict a given connection to $U$ by [[lem-a-bundle-connection-is-local-and-restricts-to-open-sets]]. Its **connection one-form in the frame $e$** is the matrix $\omega=(\omega^i{}_j)$ of scalar one-forms on $U$ characterized by
$$\nabla_X e_j=\sum_i\omega^i{}_j(X)e_i.$$
For each $j$, the smooth Hom section $\nabla e_j$ has unique fibre coordinates in $e$; these coordinates are linear in the direction and smooth, hence are scalar one-forms. Smoothness may be tested in any coordinate chart and frame, using [[prop-smoothness-of-a-section-is-equivalent-to-smooth-local-components]].

Our convention treats $e$ as a row and the coefficients $u$ of $s=eu$ as a column. A frame change is $e'=eA$ with a smooth invertible matrix $A$, so $u=Au'$ for the same section. Products of matrices and one-forms use ordinary matrix multiplication with scalar functions as coefficients. In a coordinate chart, $\omega^i{}_j=\sum_k\Gamma^i{}_{kj}\,dx^k$; this notation does not assert tensorial transformation for $\Gamma$.

For rank zero the frame and connection matrix are empty; for rank one $\omega$ is a scalar one-form. On a zero-dimensional base every one-form is zero. The frame is supplied locally, so this definition involves no global selection or existence theorem.
items.proof_plan: After restricting the connection to U, define the matrix of one-forms omega by nabla e_j=sum_i omega^i_j tensor e_i. The basis gives unique smooth coefficients. Adopt row frame e and column section coefficients, so eprime=e A.

items.title: Local coordinate formula for a bundle connection
items.statement:
In a local frame $e$, write $s=eu$ with coefficient column $u$. Then
$$\nabla_Xs=e\bigl(X(u)+\omega(X)u\bigr),\qquad \nabla s=e(du+\omega u).$$
Here the last expression means an $E$-valued one-form, and $X(u)$ and $du$ act entrywise.
items.proof_plan: Apply the directional Leibniz rule to the finite expansion s=sum_j s^j e_j. Collect coefficients: nabla_Xs=e(X(s)+omega(X)s). This applies to local sections by the locality lemma.

items.title: Connection one form transformation law
items.statement:
If $e'=eA$ are two frames on an overlap, their matrices for the same connection satisfy
$$\omega'=A^{-1}\omega A+A^{-1}dA.$$
All entries of $dA$ are differentials of scalar functions; the order of the matrix factors is as displayed.
items.proof_plan: Differentiate eprime=e A: nabla(e A)=e(omega A+dA)=eprime[A^-1 omega A+A^-1 dA]. This proves the precise inhomogeneous transformation formula in the adopted convention.

items.title: Local connection forms glue exactly when they obey the transformation law
items.statement:
Let a smooth vector bundle be covered by supplied frames $e_\alpha$ on $U_\alpha$, with $e_\beta=e_\alpha A_{\alpha\beta}$ on overlaps. Matrices of smooth one-forms $\omega_\alpha$ are the local matrices of a unique connection if and only if
$$\omega_\beta=A_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}\omega_\alpha A_{\alpha\beta}+A_{\alpha\beta}^{-1}dA_{\alpha\beta}$$
on every overlap. No local finiteness or choice assumption is required for this gluing statement.
items.proof_plan: Define the operator in each frame by ds+omega s. On overlaps s=A sprime; substituting the transformation rule gives the same section-valued one-form. Smooth local sections paste and satisfy the global Leibniz rule. Conversely an intrinsic connection forces the same rule by item 6.

items.title: The difference of two connections is an endomorphism valued one form
items.statement:
For two connections $
abla^0,
abla^1$ on the same bundle $E$, there is a unique smooth section $B$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(TM,\operatorname{End}E)$ such that
$$
abla^1_Xs-
abla^0_Xs=B(X)s.$$
This is called an endomorphism-valued one-form. In a frame it has matrix $\omega_1-\omega_0$.
items.proof_plan: Subtract the two Leibniz formulas: the df term cancels. The difference is C-infinity-linear in both X and s. In a frame its smooth matrix is omega_1-omega_0 and transforms homogeneously, hence defines an End(E)-valued one-form. Do not infer fibrewise dependence from linearity without locality/local-frame verification.

items.title: Adding an endomorphism valued one form to a connection gives a connection
items.statement:
If $
abla$ is a connection and $B\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Hom}(TM,\operatorname{End}E))$, then
$$(
abla+B)_Xs=
abla_Xs+B(X)s$$
defines a connection. If the set of connections is nonempty, it is an affine space modeled on the real vector space of endomorphism-valued one-forms: that vector space acts freely and transitively by this addition.
items.proof_plan: For A in Gamma(T*M tensor End(E)), set nablaPrime_X s=nabla_Xs+A(X)s. The added term is C-infinity-bilinear and smooth, so all directional connection laws hold. Together with the difference result this is the affine-space assertion.

items.title: Every smooth vector bundle admits a connection
items.statement: Assume AC. Every finite-rank smooth real vector bundle over a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold, with boundary allowed, admits a connection. No canonicity or smaller sufficient choice bound is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Use full AC explicitly for the arbitrary indexed choices in the published subordinate-coordinate-ball/shrinking route and for the choices of local frames and bump data. The published partition argument is used with that stronger assumption, not as a proof of its advertised AC_omega bound. Choose a locally finite smooth partition (rho_i) subordinate to bundle trivializations and the flat derivative nabla^(i) in each chosen frame. For a section s, extend rho_i nabla^(i)s by zero; this is smooth since the support of rho_i lies inside its trivializing open set. The locally finite sum defines a smooth E-valued one-form operator. R-linearity is immediate, and the Leibniz rule is sum_i rho_i (df tensor s+f nabla^(i)s)=df tensor s+f nabla s because sum_i rho_i=1. The weights multiply derivatives and are not differentiated. This proves existence, not canonicity or a minimal choice bound. Results that start with a given connection do not inherit this existence assumption.

items.title: Pullback connection
items.statement:
Let $f:N\to M$ be smooth and let $\nabla$ be a connection on $E\to M$. The bundle $f^*E$ has the smooth structure of [[thm-the-pullback-fibre-product-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]. In a pulled-back frame $f^*e$ on $f^{-1}U$, the **pullback connection** $f^*\nabla$ is specified by
$$ (f^*\nabla)_X((f^*e)u)=(f^*e)\bigl(X(u)+(f^*\omega)(X)u\bigr),$$
where $(f^*\omega)_q(v)=\omega_{f(q)}(df_qv)$ entrywise and $u$ is any smooth coefficient column on $N$. These are local prescriptions under the gluing criterion [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]]; their compatibility and hence well-definedness are proved in the next theorem.

In particular, coefficient functions are not required to factor through $f$. For constant $f$, a constant frame of $E_{f(N)}$ gives zero pulled-back matrix and ordinary differentiation of arbitrary $u$; it does not make every varying section parallel. Empty source and rank-zero bundles use empty coefficient data. No injectivity, immersion, submersion, or choice of an extension is part of this definition.
items.proof_plan: For smooth f:N->M define the connection on f*E by coefficient matrix f*omega in pulled-back frames; then differentiate arbitrary smooth coefficient functions on N. General sections of f*E are not assumed to be pullbacks of global sections of E.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control

items.title: Pullback connection is well defined and functorial
items.statement:
The pullback prescription defines a unique connection $f^*
abla$, independent of frames. Under the canonical bundle isomorphisms it satisfies $\operatorname{id}^*
abla=
abla$ and $g^*(f^*
abla)=(f\circ g)^*
abla$. For a local section $s$ of $E$,
$$ (f^*
abla)_X(f^*s)(q)=(
abla s)_{f(q)}(df_qX_q).$$
The right side is interpreted in the fibre of the pullback bundle at $q$.
items.proof_plan: The identity d(A composed f)=f*(dA) and preservation of matrix multiplication give the same transformation law for f*omega. Gluing proves frame independence. For a composite g followed by f the matrices satisfy g*(f*omega)=(f composed g)*omega, proving functoriality under the canonical bundle identifications.

items.title: Dual connection
items.statement:
The **dual connection** on the smooth bundle $E^*$ of [[thm-dual-and-hom-transition-functions-define-smooth-bundles]] is characterized by
$$ (\nabla^*_X\alpha)(s)=X(\alpha(s))-\alpha(\nabla_Xs).$$
The right side is function-linear in $s$: replacing $s$ by $fs$ introduces $X(f)\alpha(s)$ once with each sign, so those terms cancel.

Here is the construction, including well-definedness. In a frame $e$ write $s=eu$ and write $\alpha$ with dual coefficient column $a$, so $\alpha(s)=a^Tu$. The coordinate formula [[prop-local-coordinate-formula-for-a-bundle-connection]] gives
$$X(a^Tu)-a^T(X(u)+\omega(X)u)=(X(a)-\omega(X)^Ta)^Tu.$$
Thus the required coefficients are $X(a)-\omega(X)^Ta$, and the local connection matrix in the dual frame is $-\omega^T$. These local rules are smooth, real-linear and obey the section Leibniz rule by the scalar product rule. On an overlap both give the intrinsic displayed pairing formula; agreement against every local frame section forces equality of the dual covectors. They therefore glue to a connection, equivalently by [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]]. Testing against a basis also proves uniqueness. This verifies the implicit characterization rather than assuming that it defines an operator.

The derivative on scalar functions is $X(f)$; duality preserves the evaluation pairing with that scalar connection. For rank one the matrix changes sign; for rank zero evaluation and all coefficients are empty. Zero sections give zero derivatives, while empty bases give the unique operator. This construction is local and canonical from the given connection and requires no choice axiom.
items.proof_plan: Define the dual connection by X(alpha(s))=(nabla_X alpha)(s)+alpha(nabla_Xs). In dual frames its matrix is -omega transpose; this yields existence, uniqueness and the transformation law, rather than only an implicit formula.

items.title: Finite tensor products of smooth vector bundles
items.statement: For finite-rank smooth real vector bundles $E_1,\ldots,E_k$ on $M$, define the fibre tensor product to be the vector space of multilinear maps $E_{1,p}^*\times\cdots\times E_{k,p}^*\to\mathbb R$. The elementary tensor $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k$ evaluates to $\prod_j\alpha_j(v_j)$. These spaces form a canonical smooth bundle, denoted $E_1\otimes\cdots\otimes E_k$, with product frames. Every local section is a finite sum of product-frame tensors with smooth coefficients. The empty product is the trivial real line.
items.proof_plan: Completed local multilinear model and product-frame construction in canonical item.

references.title: Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, associated bundles and Example 5.1.6

items.title: Product connection on tensor and hom bundles
items.statement:
Give each of finitely many bundles $E_j$ a connection. Use the tensor bundle constructed in [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]], including its multilinear model on the dual fibres. The **product connection** is characterized on local elementary tensors by
$$\nabla_X(s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k)=\sum_j s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\nabla^j_Xs_j\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k.$$
For the empty product, the connection on scalar functions is $\nabla_Xf=X(f)$.

To construct it without a decomposition assumption, for a multilinear-model section $T$ and local dual sections $\alpha_j$ put
$$(\nabla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)=X\bigl(T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)\bigr)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,(\nabla^j)^*_X\alpha_j,\ldots,\alpha_k).$$
Use the dual connections of [[def-dual-connection]]. Multiplying any argument by a smooth $f$ produces two opposite $X(f)T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ terms; thus this expression is function-linear in every dual argument. In dual frames its coefficients are smooth and depend only on their fibre values, so it defines a smooth tensor section. The same intrinsic expression on overlaps gives agreement. Its real-linearity, function-linearity in $X$, and rule $\nabla_X(fT)=X(f)T+f\nabla_XT$ follow by direct expansion, establishing the connection. This also gives the gluing criterion of [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]].

On a pure tensor, the scalar product rule and the dual pairing identity reduce this expression to the first displayed sum. Hence it respects the balanced identity $(fs)\otimes t=s\otimes(ft)$: either derivative gives the same term $X(f)s\otimes t$ and the same two terms multiplied by $f$. Every section has a finite local product-frame expansion, so that rule and the connection Leibniz identity force uniqueness.

For bundles $E,F$, identify $F\otimes E^*$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)$ by $t\otimes\alpha\mapsto(v\mapsto\alpha(v)t)$. In local bases these elementary tensors are precisely the matrix units, proving this is a smooth fibrewise isomorphism. The induced **Hom connection** is therefore
$$(\nabla_XA)(s)=\nabla^F_X(A(s))-A(\nabla^E_Xs).$$
The two $X(f)A(s)$ terms cancel when $s$ is replaced by $fs$, ensuring a fibrewise map. Rank-zero factors give zero bundles, whereas the empty product is the scalar line; these conventions are different. No choice beyond finitely many local frames is needed.
items.proof_plan: On tensor products set nabla_X(s tensor t)=nabla_Xs tensor t+s tensor nabla_Xt; enforce the balanced relation (fs) tensor t=s tensor (ft). Define Hom using F tensor E* and obtain nabla_X A(s)=nabla_X(A(s))-A(nabla_Xs). Local matrices prove smoothness and gluing.

items.title: Induced connections commute with contraction and permutation
items.statement:
For the induced tensor connections, every fixed permutation $	au$ of tensor slots intertwines covariant differentiation. So does any contraction $C$ of an $E^*$ slot against an $E$ slot equipped with dual connections:
$$
abla_X(	au T)=	au(
abla_XT),\qquad 
abla_X(CT)=C(
abla_XT).$$
A full contraction takes values in scalar functions, with derivative $X$.
items.proof_plan: On pure tensors, differentiate each slot once. The two terms involving a contracted dual/primal slot combine to the derivative of their pairing by the dual formula. Reordering slots commutes with the sum. Local frames span all sections, so the identities extend.

items.title: Induced connection on exterior powers is a degree zero derivation
items.statement:
A connection on $E$ induces a connection on each $ igwedge^kE$, including the scalar bundle $ igwedge^0E$. For sections $S$ and $T$ of exterior degrees $p$ and $q$,
$$
abla_X(S\wedge T)=(
abla_XS)\wedge T+S\wedge(
abla_XT).$$
There is no graded sign: the covariant derivative in a fixed direction has degree zero.
items.proof_plan: The tensor connection commutes with alternating projection, hence restricts to exterior powers. Expanding a wedge gives nabla_X(alpha wedge beta)=nabla_Xalpha wedge beta+alpha wedge nabla_Xbeta, with no Koszul sign because this derivative has degree zero.

items.title: Vector field and section along a smooth curve
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be smooth, with smooth local extensions at any included endpoints. A **section of $E$ along $\gamma$** is a smooth section of $\gamma^*E$ as constructed in [[thm-the-pullback-fibre-product-is-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]. Equivalently it is a smooth map $V:I\to E$ with $\pi(V(t))=\gamma(t)$. For $E=TM$ it is a **vector field along $\gamma$**. In a pulled-back frame it has the form $V(t)=\sum_jv^j(t)e_j(\gamma(t))$ with arbitrary smooth coefficients $v^j$.

Values belong to the fibre over the parameter value, even if $\gamma(t)=\gamma(u)$ for $t\ne u$. For example, for a constant curve at $p$ and $v\ne0$ in $E_p$, the section $V(t)=tv$ is allowed and cannot be $s\circ\gamma$ for an ambient section $s$. Thus an ambient extension is not part of this definition.

For a piecewise smooth curve on a compact interval, use a finite subdivision into smooth pieces (each smooth up to its endpoints). A piecewise smooth section is continuous on the whole interval and smooth on each piece. On a singleton interval it is just a fibre vector; on an empty interval it is the empty section. These conventions define sections, without attempting differentiation on a singleton.
items.proof_plan: A section along a smooth curve gamma:I->M is a smooth section of gamma*E. In particular it can vary along a constant curve or take different values at different parameter points mapping to the same base point; an ambient extension is not assumed.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 17; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Covariant derivative along a curve
items.statement:
For a given connection on $E$ and a smooth curve on an interval with nonempty interior, the **covariant derivative along the curve** is
$$D_tV=(\gamma^*\nabla)_{\partial/\partial t}V.$$
Here $V$ is a section of the pullback bundle as in [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]], and the pullback connection exists by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It is real-linear and satisfies $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for functions of the parameter.

At an included endpoint the smooth up-to-boundary coefficients have their one-sided derivative; equivalently any smooth local extension of the coefficients gives this value, because extensions agreeing on a one-sided interval have the same derivative there. For a piecewise smooth curve the derivative is defined on each piece, with separate one-sided derivatives at corners; those derivatives are not required to agree. A singleton interval carries no derivative operator under this convention and will have identity transport by definition. A zero section or a rank-zero bundle gives zero covariant derivative. Constant base curves can have sections with nonzero coefficient derivative.
items.proof_plan: Take the pullback connection on gamma*E and evaluate on partial_t, defining D_t. On a closed interval use smooth extensions locally at endpoints; only one-sided values are needed for transport.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 18; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Covariant derivative along a curve is independent of frame and extension
items.statement:
The operator $D_t$ is independent of local frames. If $V=s\circ\gamma$ near a parameter value for an ambient local section $s$, then
$$D_tV=(\nabla s)_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t)).$$
Consequently any two such extensions give the same derivative. This is an agreement assertion when an ambient extension exists, not an assertion that every section along a curve extends.
items.proof_plan: Pullback well-definedness proves frame independence. When a section actually is the pullback of an ambient section, the formula agrees with nabla_dotgamma; chain rule shows independence of any such extension. Do not claim every along-curve section admits an ambient extension: a nonconstant coefficient over a constant curve is a counterexample.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 19; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Local frame formula for covariant differentiation along a curve
items.statement:
If $V(t)=e(\gamma(t))v(t)$ and $B(t)=\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))$, then
$$D_tV=e(\gamma(t))(v'(t)+B(t)v(t)).$$
Thus $D_tV=0$ is the linear system $v'=-Bv$.
items.proof_plan: Writing V=e(gamma(t))v(t) gives D_tV=e(gamma(t))[vprime+omega(dotgamma)v]. Under eprime=e A, differentiate v=A(gamma)vprime and use the inhomogeneous connection law to verify covariance explicitly.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 20; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Parallel section along a curve
items.statement:
A section $V$ along a smooth curve is **parallel** if $D_tV=0$. By [[prop-local-frame-formula-for-covariant-differentiation-along-a-curve]], in a pulled-back frame this means
$$v'(t)=-\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))v(t).$$
For a piecewise smooth curve, parallel means continuous on the full parameter interval and parallel on each smooth piece. One-sided derivatives are used at the endpoints of a piece; no equality of the two derivatives at a corner is required. On a singleton, every prescribed fibre vector is a parallel section by convention; on an empty interval the empty section is parallel.

The zero section is parallel, and along a constant curve the coefficients in a constant fibre frame are constant precisely for parallel sections. The definition does not assert that all local coefficients in arbitrary moving frames are constant.
items.proof_plan: A parallel section satisfies D_tV=0, equivalently vprime=-omega(dotgamma)v in each local frame.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 21; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of parallel sections
items.statement: Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be smooth on an interval, with smooth one-sided data at included endpoints. For every $t_0\in I$ and $v_0\in E_{\gamma(t_0)}$ there is exactly one parallel section $V$ on all of $I$ with $V(t_0)=v_0$. The same holds for a piecewise smooth curve on a compact interval, with continuity at its finitely many corners. A singleton carries its prescribed vector. No AC is required for a supplied connection and curve.
items.proof_plan: On each compact frame subinterval solve vprime=B(t)v with B=-omega(dotgamma). The published matrix ODE lemma supplies solutions on the whole subinterval, not just germ existence. A finite subdivision subordinate to the pulled-back trivializations permits endpoint patching; uniqueness identifies all overlaps. Smoothness follows from the smooth equation. On general intervals use uniqueness to unite compact subinterval solutions.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 22; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Parallel transport along a piecewise smooth curve
items.statement:
For a piecewise smooth curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ and $v\in E_{\gamma(a)}$, let $V_v$ be the unique continuous piecewise parallel section with $V_v(a)=v$, supplied by [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-parallel-sections]]. Its **parallel transport** is
$$P_\gamma:E_{\gamma(a)}\to E_{\gamma(b)},\qquad P_\gamma(v)=V_v(b).$$
More generally, $P_{\gamma;s,t}$ sends initial data at $s$ to its value at $t$, allowing either order of the parameters. The same theorem gives independence from frames and subdivisions. On a singleton, $P_\gamma$ is the identity of its fibre. An empty curve has no endpoint fibres and is not assigned such a map. Zero initial data maps to zero; the transport depends on the supplied connection as well as the curve. Linearity and invertibility are proved next.
items.proof_plan: For a continuous curve with a finite piecewise-smooth subdivision define P_gamma(v) by the unique continuous parallel section with initial value v, smooth on pieces. Refining the partition gives the same section by uniqueness. Include stationary pieces and the zero-length constant path.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 23; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Parallel transport is a linear isomorphism
items.statement:
For each curve under the transport definition, $P_{\gamma;s,t}$ is a linear isomorphism and
$$P_{\gamma;s,t}^{-1}=P_{\gamma;t,s}.$$
For the reversed curve $\bar\gamma(u)=\gamma(a+b-u)$, $P_{\bar\gamma}=P_\gamma^{-1}$.
items.proof_plan: Linear combinations of solutions solve the same homogeneous system. Transport along reversal solves the reversed equation by chain rule, and concatenating a curve with its reversal yields the identity by uniqueness. Thus P_gamma is a linear isomorphism with inverse P_reverse.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 24; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Parallel transport under reparametrization reversal and concatenation
items.statement:
An increasing smooth surjective reparametrization $h:[c,d]\to[a,b]$, allowing $h'=0$, leaves endpoint transport unchanged. A decreasing one reverses it. If $\gamma_1$ ends where $\gamma_2$ starts, their concatenation, traversing $\gamma_1$ first, satisfies
$$P_{\gamma_2*\gamma_1}=P_{\gamma_2}\circ P_{\gamma_1},\qquad P_{\bar\gamma}=P_\gamma^{-1}.$$
These assertions include piecewise smooth reparametrizations when the composed curves admit finite smooth subdivisions, as well as inserted constant pauses.
items.proof_plan: Apply the chain rule to a smooth monotone time change, allowing vanishing derivative: D_t(V composed h)=hprime(D_s V) composed h. Endpoint transport is unchanged for orientation-preserving reparametrizations. Reversal yields inverse and concatenation yields P_second composed P_first. Prove the finite-piece extensions by refinement.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 25; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Pullback connections intertwine parallel transport
items.statement:
For $f:N\to M$ smooth and $\gamma:[a,b]\to N$ piecewise smooth, let $J_t:(f^*E)_{\gamma(t)}\to E_{f(\gamma(t))}$ be the canonical fibre identification. Then
$$J_bP^{f^*\nabla}_\gamma=P^\nabla_{f\circ\gamma}J_a.$$
items.proof_plan: For gamma in N, the coefficient ODE for f*connection along gamma has matrix (f*omega)(dotgamma)=omega(d f dotgamma). This is exactly the ODE along f composed gamma. Uniqueness identifies transport under the canonical endpoint fibre maps.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 26; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Metric compatible connection on a riemannian vector bundle
items.statement:
Let $h$ be a supplied smooth positive-definite bundle metric, as in [[def-smooth-bundle-metric]]. A connection is **metric compatible** if, for all local smooth sections $s,t$ and local vector fields $X$,
$$X(h(s,t))=h(\nabla_Xs,t)+h(s,\nabla_Xt).$$
Local connection operations are provided by [[prop-connection-laws-in-directional-form]]. Equivalently, the induced connection on $E^*\otimes E^*$ annihilates $h$: by [[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]], its evaluation is exactly the left side minus the right side. Thus $\nabla h=0$ is a specified identity of tensors, not an independent assumption about an endomorphism.

In a local frame write $h(e_i,e_j)=H_{ij}$. Testing on frame sections gives $X(H)=\omega(X)^TH+H\omega(X)$; conversely expanding $s=eu,t=ev$ and using the scalar product rule gives the full identity from this matrix equation. This makes the condition pointwise testable in the direction and the two section values. Rank zero satisfies it vacuously. A metric is supplied, so metric existence and its choice requirements are not used.
items.proof_plan: For a supplied positive definite smooth fibre metric, require X<h(s),t> interpreted as X h(s,t)=h(nabla_Xs,t)+h(s,nabla_Xt) for all sections and fields. Equivalently the induced connection annihilates h; correct notation is h(s,t), not an endomorphism h(s).

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 27; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: A connection is metric compatible iff parallel transport is isometric
items.statement: A connection on a bundle with supplied positive-definite metric $h$ is metric compatible if and only if parallel transport along every piecewise smooth compact-interval curve is an isometry of endpoint fibres. Manifolds with boundary are included.
items.proof_plan: Compatibility makes the derivative of h(V,W) vanish for parallel V,W, so transport is isometric. Conversely, along any curve through p choose a parallel frame by transporting a basis; isometry makes its Gram matrix constant. Differentiate arbitrary coefficient expansions to get the compatibility identity at p for every tangent direction (one-sided curves suffice at boundary points).

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 28; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Affine connection on a smooth manifold
items.statement:
An **affine connection** on a smooth manifold $M$ is a connection on the tangent bundle $TM$ in the sense of [[def-connection-on-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]. Thus it assigns a vector field $
abla_XY$ to two vector fields and is function-linear in the differentiating direction $X$, real-linear in $Y$, and obeys $
abla_X(fY)=X(f)Y+f
abla_XY$.

The word affine imposes neither a metric nor torsion freeness. The tangent-bundle specialization allows the Lie bracket of $X,Y$ to be compared with their covariant derivatives; there is no corresponding bracket on sections of a general vector bundle. Manifolds with boundary are allowed, and tangent vectors at their boundary need not be tangent to the boundary. The empty and zero-dimensional manifolds have the unique tangent-bundle connection.
items.proof_plan: An affine connection on M is a connection on TM. This is a specialization of bundle connection; torsion below uses the tangent-bundle identification and Lie bracket.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 29; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Christoffel symbols of an affine connection
items.statement:
For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.
items.proof_plan: In a coordinate frame define Gamma^k_ij by nabla_partial_i partial_j=Gamma^k_ij partial_k; the first lower index is the differentiation direction.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 30; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Christoffel symbol transformation law
items.statement:
For coordinates $x^i$ and $y^a$, the symbols transform by
$$\widetilde\Gamma^c{}_{ab}=\frac{\partial y^c}{\partial x^k}\left(\frac{\partial x^i}{\partial y^a}\frac{\partial x^j}{\partial y^b}\Gamma^k{}_{ij}+\frac{\partial^2x^k}{\partial y^a\partial y^b}\right).$$
Repeated indices are summed. The second-derivative term is inhomogeneous.
items.proof_plan: For x=x(y), expand nabla_partial_ya partial_yb using the Leibniz rule. Obtain GammaPrime^c_ab=(partial y^c/partial x^k)[Gamma^k_ij(partial x^i/partial y^a)(partial x^j/partial y^b)+partial^2 x^k/(partial y^a partial y^b)]. The Hessian term is essential.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 31; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Torsion tensor of an affine connection
items.statement:
For an affine connection, define its **torsion** on local vector fields by
$$T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y].$$
The connection is as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]], and the bracket is the smooth vector field given by [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]]. The next lemma proves this operation is a smooth alternating tangent-valued two-tensor. It is called **torsion free** when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all local fields.

This construction uses the tangent bundle: general bundle sections have no Lie bracket with which to form this difference. In dimension zero all terms vanish. Smooth fields on a manifold with boundary need not be boundary-tangent; bracket and covariant derivative use smooth coordinate derivatives there as well.
items.proof_plan: Set T(X,Y)=nabla_XY-nabla_YX-[X,Y]. This definition is restricted to affine connections; a general vector bundle has no such bracket of its sections.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 32; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Torsion is c infinity bilinear and skew symmetric
items.statement: Torsion is $C^\infty(M)$-bilinear and skew-symmetric, and determines a smooth section of $\operatorname{Hom}(\bigwedge^2TM,TM)$, equivalently an alternating tensor of type $(1,2)$.
items.proof_plan: Expand T(fX,Y) and T(X,fY). The derivative-of-f terms from nabla cancel those from the bracket. Skew symmetry is immediate on exchanging X,Y. Smooth frame coefficients then define a (1,2) tensor.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 33; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Torsion free is equivalent to symmetric christoffel symbols in coordinate frames
items.statement: An affine connection is torsion free if and only if in every coordinate chart $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}=\Gamma^k{}_{ji}$ for all indices. It suffices to check this on a coordinate-chart cover. This criterion concerns coordinate frames.
items.proof_plan: Coordinate vector fields commute, so T(partial_i,partial_j)=(Gamma^k_ij-Gamma^k_ji)partial_k. Tensoriality implies vanishing on that frame is equivalent to T=0. The coordinate-frame qualification cannot be omitted.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 34; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Levi civita connection
items.statement:
For a supplied Riemannian metric $g$, a **Levi–Civita connection** is an affine connection on $TM$ that is both metric compatible and torsion free, in the senses of [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]], [[def-metric-compatible-connection-on-a-riemannian-vector-bundle]] and [[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]]. Thus for all local fields
$$Xg(Y,Z)=g(
abla_XY,Z)+g(Y,
abla_XZ),\qquad 
abla_XY-
abla_YX=[X,Y].$$
Existence and uniqueness are proved below from the supplied metric by the Koszul formula. This definition does not choose an arbitrary connection first and does not assume the general connection-existence theorem. In dimension zero the unique tangent-bundle connection satisfies both identities; in dimension one torsion freeness alone imposes no restriction, so metric compatibility remains essential.
items.proof_plan: A Levi-Civita connection for a supplied Riemannian metric is an affine connection that is metric compatible and has zero torsion. Existence is a later theorem, not assumed by this predicate.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 35; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Koszul formula is necessary for a levi civita connection
items.statement:
Every Levi–Civita connection obeys the Koszul formula
$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z),$$
where
$$K(X,Y,Z)=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)-g(X,[Y,Z])+g(Y,[Z,X])+g(Z,[X,Y]).$$
The right side uses only the supplied metric and vector fields.
items.proof_plan: Write metric compatibility for Xg(Y,Z), Yg(Z,X), Zg(X,Y); add the first two and subtract the third. Replace reversed derivatives using zero torsion and collect to obtain 2g(nabla_XY,Z)=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)-g(X,[Y,Z])+g(Y,[Z,X])+g(Z,[X,Y]). Nondegeneracy gives uniqueness.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 36; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: The koszul formula defines an affine connection
items.statement:
For any supplied smooth Riemannian metric, its Koszul expression $K$ determines a unique smooth affine connection by
$$\nabla_XY=\left(\tfrac12 K(X,Y,\mathord\cdot)\right)^\sharp.$$
This construction works on manifolds with boundary and requires no AC.
items.proof_plan: Use the displayed Koszul expression K(X,Y,Z) as a formula, not an already-existing connection. Expand brackets to prove K is C-infinity-linear in Z and X, and K(X,fY,Z)=f K(X,Y,Z)+2X(f)g(Y,Z). Thus K/2 is a smooth one-form in Z and sharp defines a smooth nabla_XY satisfying the connection axioms. The use of item 36 here is only its algebraic formula; its existence hypothesis is not inferred.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 37; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Fundamental theorem of riemannian geometry
items.statement: Every supplied smooth Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold, including a manifold with boundary, has exactly one Levi–Civita connection. The construction adds no choice assumption.
items.proof_plan: Subtract K(X,Y,Z)-K(Y,X,Z) to get 2g([X,Y],Z), proving zero torsion. Add K(X,Y,Z)+K(X,Z,Y) to get 2Xg(Y,Z), proving compatibility. Item 36 gives uniqueness. All constructions are canonical from a supplied metric and add no choice.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 38; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Christoffel formula for the levi civita connection
items.statement:
In coordinates for a Riemannian metric with matrix $(g_{ij})$ and inverse $(g^{ij})$, its Levi–Civita symbols are
$$\Gamma^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12\sum_\ell g^{k\ell}(\partial_i g_{j\ell}+\partial_j g_{i\ell}-\partial_\ell g_{ij}).$$
items.proof_plan: Substitute commuting coordinate fields into Koszul and multiply by g inverse: Gamma^k_ij=one-half g^{kl}(partial_i g_jl+partial_j g_il-partial_l g_ij). Smoothness follows from invertibility of the positive definite metric matrix.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 39; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Levi civita parallel transport preserves lengths angles and volume
items.statement: Levi–Civita parallel transport preserves inner products, lengths, angles of nonzero vectors, and Riemannian volume density. If the manifold is oriented, it also preserves its oriented Riemannian volume form. Without a supplied global orientation only density preservation is claimed.
items.proof_plan: Isometric transport preserves lengths and inner products, hence angles of nonzero vectors and positive volume densities. On an oriented manifold, a continuously parallel orthonormal frame retains its orientation, giving preservation of the oriented volume form. Without orientation only density preservation is claimed.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 40; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Levi civita connection commutes with musical isomorphisms
items.statement:
For Levi–Civita and its dual connection,
$$(
abla_X\alpha)^\sharp=
abla_X(\alpha^\sharp),\qquad 
abla_X(Y^ lat)=(
abla_XY)^ lat.$$
items.proof_plan: Differentiate alpha(Y)=g(alphaSharp,Y) and cancel the terms containing nabla_XY using metric compatibility and the dual-connection rule. Nondegeneracy yields (nabla_X alpha)Sharp=nabla_X(alphaSharp). The flat identity follows by inversion.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 41; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Gradient hessian and divergence connection formulas
items.statement:
For Levi–Civita, $\operatorname{grad}f=(df)^\sharp$ and the Hessian defined by $\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\operatorname{grad}f,Y)$ is a smooth covariant two-tensor satisfying
$$\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=X(Yf)-(\nabla_XY)f,\qquad (\operatorname{Hess}f)_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_jf-\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_kf.$$
Moreover the previously defined Riemannian divergence satisfies
$$\operatorname{div}_gX=\operatorname{tr}(v\mapsto\nabla_vX)=\partial_iX^i+\Gamma^i{}_{ik}X^k.$$
items.proof_plan: Define Hess f(X,Y)=g(nabla_X grad f,Y); use metric compatibility to obtain X(Yf)-(nabla_XY)f and the coordinate formula partial_i partial_j f-Gamma^k_ij partial_k f. Trace Y->nabla_YX gives partial_i X^i+Gamma^i_ik X^k. Substitute Christoffels and the determinant derivative identity to identify this with the existing density divergence; no normal coordinates or future geodesic theorem is used.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 42; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: The riemannian hessian is symmetric
items.statement: For a smooth function $f$ on a Riemannian manifold, the Levi–Civita Hessian is symmetric: $\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hess}f(Y,X)$ for all local smooth vector fields.
items.proof_plan: Subtract Hess f(X,Y)-Hess f(Y,X)=[X,Y]f-(nabla_XY-nabla_YX)f=-df(T(X,Y))=0 for Levi-Civita. This proves symmetry without commuting arbitrary vector fields.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 43; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: Holonomy of a connection
items.statement:
For a supplied point $p$ and connection on $E$, define $\operatorname{Hol}_p(\nabla)\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(E_p)$ to be the set of transports around finite piecewise smooth loops based at $p$. Transports are invertible by [[thm-parallel-transport-is-a-linear-isomorphism]]. The constant loop gives the identity; if $A=P_\alpha$ and $B=P_\beta$, traversing $\beta$ then $\alpha$ gives $AB$; reversal of $\alpha$ gives $A^{-1}$. These assertions follow from [[prop-parallel-transport-under-reparametrization-reversal-and-concatenation]], and prove that this set is a subgroup, with associativity inherited from composition of linear maps.

A singleton constant loop suffices for nonemptiness; in rank zero this group consists of the unique automorphism of the zero vector space. There is no such pointed definition on an empty base without a point $p$. No simultaneous choice of loops representing all elements is required: closure checks two supplied representatives. The definition asserts neither homotopy invariance nor path independence. Curvature descriptions and classification of holonomy are deferred.
items.proof_plan: Define holonomy at p as the subset of GL(E_p) consisting of transports along piecewise smooth loops at p. Constant loop, concatenation and reversal prove the group axioms. This does not imply homotopy invariance. Defer Ambrose-Singer and classification to later holonomy theory; no curvature result is used.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 item 44; Datar §§5.1–5.2 and 10.1–10.3; complete source-reading still held

items.title: A connection is c infinity linear in the section being differentiated
items.statement: For every connection, $\nabla_X(fs)=f\nabla_Xs$ for all smooth $f$, vector fields $X$ and sections $s$.
items.proof_plan: On the trivial real line bundle over R with nabla=d, nabla_partial_x(x*1)=1 but x*nabla_partial_x(1)=0.

items.title: Christoffel symbols are components of a tensor
items.statement: The Christoffel symbols of any affine connection are the components of a tensor of type $(1,2)$.
items.proof_plan: For the flat connection in x on x>0, set x=exp(y). The one-dimensional transformation gives GammaPrime=1 although Gamma=0, impossible for tensorial transformation of zero.

references.locator: DG-19 false-statement inventory; elementary coordinate witnesses

items.title: Parallel transport depends only on the endpoints of a curve
items.statement: For any connection, two piecewise smooth curves with the same starting and ending points have the same parallel transport.
items.proof_plan: On the trivial real line bundle over R^2 with connection d+x dy, transport around the positively oriented unit square multiplies by exp(-1), while the constant loop gives 1. Compute the four scalar ODEs directly; no curvature theorem is needed.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 false-statement inventory; elementary coordinate witnesses

items.title: Every affine connection is the levi civita connection of a riemannian metric
items.statement: Every affine connection is the Levi–Civita connection of some Riemannian metric.
items.proof_plan: On R^2 define nabla_partial_x partial_y=partial_x and all other coordinate derivatives zero. Its torsion on (partial_x,partial_y) is partial_x, so it cannot be Levi-Civita for any metric.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 false-statement inventory; elementary coordinate witnesses

items.title: Torsion free means curvature free
items.statement:
For an affine connection define $R(X,Y)Z=
abla_X
abla_YZ-
abla_Y
abla_XZ-
abla_{[X,Y]}Z$. Call it curvature free when this expression vanishes identically. The assertion that every torsion-free connection is curvature free is false, even for Levi–Civita connections on the plane.
items.proof_plan: First supply the local meaning and invariance of R, rather than cite the later DG-21 curvature theory. The displayed commutator uses intrinsic covariant derivatives and the Lie bracket. In R(fX,Y)Z, the -(Yf)nabla_X Z from differentiating f cancels the +(Yf)nabla_X Z from [fX,Y]=f[X,Y]-(Yf)X; hence it equals fR(X,Y)Z. Skew symmetry gives linearity in Y. Expanding the two iterated derivatives on fZ gives second-derivative term (X(Yf)-Y(Xf))Z=[X,Y](f)Z, canceled by the bracket derivative, while the two cross first-derivative terms cancel pairwise. Thus R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z. Additivity and real linearity follow from the connection laws. In local smooth frames these identities express R through smooth coefficients and pointwise components of X,Y,Z, so it is an intrinsic smooth tensor and its vanishing is frame-independent. Now take g=exp(2x^2)(dx^2+dy^2) on R^2. Its Levi–Civita coefficients from the preceding formula are Gamma^x_xx=2x, Gamma^x_yy=-2x, Gamma^y_xy=Gamma^y_yx=2x, and the other coefficients are zero. They are symmetric in the lower indices, so torsion vanishes. Since coordinate fields commute, nabla_x nabla_y partial_y=(-2-4x^2)partial_x, whereas nabla_y nabla_x partial_y=-4x^2 partial_x. Consequently R(partial_x,partial_y)partial_y=-2partial_x, in particular nonzero at x=0. No Gauss–Bonnet, holonomy theorem, Bianchi identity or later curvature supplier is used; DG-21 retains the full curvature development.

items.title: Every connection on a riemannian vector bundle is metric compatible
items.statement: Every connection on a vector bundle equipped with a Riemannian bundle metric is compatible with that metric.
items.proof_plan: On the trivial real line over R with usual fibre metric, connection d+dx has nabla_partial_x 1=1. The derivative of h(1,1)=1 is zero but the compatibility RHS is 2.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 false-statement inventory; elementary coordinate witnesses

title: Connections Levi Civita and Parallel Transport — Examples

items.title: The flat connection on a trivial vector bundle
items.statement: On a supplied trivial bundle $E=M\times\mathbb R^r$, the constant frame $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ defines the flat connection $\nabla_X(\sum_a u^ae_a)=\sum_a X(u^a)e_a$. Its connection matrix is zero. Here flatness can be checked directly by the vanishing of the commutator expression below.
items.proof_plan: On M times R^r, define nabla_Xs by componentwise derivatives. Its matrix in the constant frame is zero and the Leibniz identity follows componentwise.

references.title: DG-19 design; Datar control
references.locator: DG-19 B inventory; direct coordinate/ODE verification

items.title: A connection one form on a trivial line bundle
items.statement:
For any supplied smooth one-form $a$ on $M$, $
abla(ue)=(du+au)e$ is a connection on $M	imes\mathbb R$, where $e$ is the constant unit frame. Its connection form is $a$. In particular $a=x\,dy$ on $\mathbb R^2$ gives $
abla_{\partial_x}(ue)=\partial_xu\,e$ and $
abla_{\partial_y}(ue)=(\partial_yu+xu)e$.
items.proof_plan: For a smooth one-form a on M, the rule nabla s=ds+a s defines a line-bundle connection in its global frame. Choosing a=x dy on R^2 gives a concrete nontrivial coefficient.

items.title: Gauge transformation of a connection one form
items.statement: On an open set with a real line-bundle frame $e$ and connection form $\omega$, change frame to $e'=e\exp(f)$ for a smooth real function $f$. Then $\omega'=\omega+df$. Thus zero coefficients can become nonzero without changing the connection.
items.proof_plan: On a real line bundle change frame eprime=e exp(f). Then Aprime formula gives omegaPrime=omega+df; for omega=0,f=x the new coefficient is dx although the intrinsic connection is unchanged.

items.title: Pullback of the flat connection
items.statement: For a smooth map $f:N\to M$, the pullback of the flat connection on $M\times\mathbb R^r$ is the componentwise derivative on the canonically identified product $f^*(M\times\mathbb R^r)=N\times\mathbb R^r$.
items.proof_plan: Pull back the constant frame and zero connection matrix of a trivial bundle along f:N->M; f*0=0, so the pulled-back connection is the componentwise derivative in that pulled-back frame.

items.title: Parallel transport for a scalar linear ode
items.statement:
On a framed real line bundle along a curve over $[a,b]$, let the scalar connection coefficient evaluated on velocity be $c(t)$, continuous on each of finitely many smooth pieces. Then the parallel equation is $v'=-c(t)v$ and endpoint transport in this frame is
$$v(b)=\exp\left(-\int_a^b c(t)\,dt\right)v(a).$$
items.proof_plan: Solve vprime=-a(t)v: v(b)=exp(-integral_a^b a(t)dt)v(a). Verify the derivative and initial condition; zero input gives zero and reversal changes the exponent sign.

items.title: The euclidean levi civita connection
items.statement: The Euclidean metric on $\mathbb R^n$ has Levi–Civita derivative $\nabla_XY=\sum_jX(Y^j)\partial_j$ in Cartesian coordinates. Its Christoffel symbols vanish, and parallel transport along every piecewise smooth curve preserves the Cartesian components.
items.proof_plan: For Euclidean coordinates g_ij=delta_ij all derivatives of g vanish, so every Christoffel symbol is zero and parallel vectors have constant components.

items.title: Christoffel symbols in polar coordinates
items.statement: For the Euclidean plane in a polar chart $(r,\theta)$ with $r>0$, the metric is $dr^2+r^2d\theta^2$. Its only nonzero Levi–Civita symbols are $\Gamma^r{}_{\theta\theta}=-r$ and $\Gamma^\theta{}_{r\theta}=\Gamma^\theta{}_{\theta r}=1/r$.
items.proof_plan: For g=dr^2+r^2 dtheta^2 on r>0 obtain Gamma^r_theta theta=-r and Gamma^theta_r theta=Gamma^theta_theta r=1/r, all others zero. State the chart excludes r=0.

items.title: Levi civita connection of a conformal plane metric
items.statement:
For a smooth real function $u$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, the metric $g=e^{2u}(dx^2+dy^2)$ has
$$\Gamma^k{}_{ij}=\delta^k_j u_i+\delta^k_i u_j-\delta_{ij}u_k,$$
where $u_i=\partial_i u$ and the last index uses the Cartesian Euclidean convention. For $u=x^2$, the nonzero entries are $\Gamma^x{}_{xx}=2x$, $\Gamma^x{}_{yy}=-2x$, $\Gamma^y{}_{xy}=\Gamma^y{}_{yx}=2x$.
items.proof_plan: For g=exp(2u)(dx^2+dy^2), substitute into Christoffels to get Gamma^k_ij=delta^k_j u_i+delta^k_i u_j-delta_ij u_k. Give u=x^2 as a nonconstant smooth example.

items.title: Parallel transport on the round sphere along the equator
items.statement: On the unit round sphere $S^2$, the Levi–Civita derivative is $\nabla_XY=D_XY+\langle X,Y\rangle p$, where $p$ is the position vector and $D_XY$ differentiates the three ambient component functions of the tangent field $Y$. Along the equator $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$, the fields $T(t)=(-\sin t,\cos t,0)$ and $N(t)=(0,0,1)$ are parallel. Thus transport around $0\leq t\leq2\pi$ is the identity.
items.proof_plan: On the unit sphere the projected ambient derivative nabla_XY=D_XY+<X,Y>p is tangent, compatible and torsion free; Levi-Civita uniqueness identifies it. Along gamma(t)=(cos t,sin t,0), the tangent (-sin t,cos t,0) and constant (0,0,1) are parallel, so full equatorial-loop transport is the identity.

items.title: A torsion free connection that is not metric compatible
items.statement: A torsion-free affine connection on a Riemannian manifold must be compatible with the supplied Riemannian metric.
items.proof_plan: On R with g=dx^2 take Gamma^1_11=1. Torsion vanishes in dimension one, while compatibility fails since partial_x g(1,1)=0 and the derivative RHS is 2. No claim that this connection is incompatible with every possible metric.

items.title: Path dependent parallel transport on the sphere
items.statement: Levi–Civita parallel transport on the unit round sphere depends only on the two endpoints.
items.proof_plan: Compute the same projected connection on the three quarter great circles from e1 to e2 to e3 to e1. Along each arc its tangent and fixed normal are parallel. Starting vector e2 ends as e3 at e1; the constant loop fixes e2. This is explicit path dependence, without Gauss-Bonnet or a curvature/holonomy theorem.

items.title: Hessian and divergence in euclidean coordinates
items.statement:
In Cartesian coordinates on Euclidean $\mathbb R^n$, $(\operatorname{Hess}f)_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j f$ and $\operatorname{div}X=\sum_i\partial_iX^i$. For $f(x,y)=x^2y$ and $X=x^2\partial_x+xy\partial_y$, these become
$$\operatorname{Hess}f=\begin{pmatrix}2y&2x\\2x&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \operatorname{div}X=3x.$$
items.proof_plan: Euclidean g has zero Christoffels. Hence Hess f has entries partial_i partial_j f and div X=sum_i partial_i X^i. For f=x^2 y in R^2, Hess=[[2y,2x],[2x,0]], and X=(x^2,xy) has divergence 3x.
